articles.title: Costs and imaging delays associated with acute reactions to contrast material: A single-center retrospective study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Acute reactions to iodinated contrast material (ICM) and gadolinium-based contrast agents (GBCAs) are routinely encountered during CT and MR exams, but their associated direct medical costs and radiology practice workflow delays remain largely unknown. The purpose of this five-year, single-center retrospective study was to determine the costs and the Radiology departmental delays associated with acute ICM and GBCA reactions. METHODS: Contrast-enhanced CT and MR (CECT and CEMR) examinations performed from November 1, 2019, to October 31, 2024 at our institution were included. Acute reactions were identified as allergic-like or physiologic and categorized by severity using established ACR criteria. Drug, procedural, and hospitalization costs were estimated using 2025 CMS and US Department of Veterans Affairs databases. Delays were quantified by comparing time from exam start to departmental exit for exams with and without reactions. RESULTS: A total of 363,671 CECT exams and 253,860 CEMR exams were included, with 1099 acute ICM (789 allergic-like, 310 physiologic) and 521 acute GBCA reactions (321 allergic-like, 200 physiologic) identified. A minority of patients received billable medication or a procedure for their treatment (321 CECT, 29%; 107 CEMR, 21%). Median costs were modest ($15 for CECT; $1.66 for CEMR), but varied substantially by severity (severe reactions up to $238,029) and outcome (ED patient = $326, Admitted patient = $13,942). Acute ICM and GBCA reactions resulted in a median additional time of 25 minutes (IQR 11-43 min) and 27 minutes (IQR 8-59 min) in Radiology, respectively. CONCLUSION: Acute ICM and GBCA reactions contribute to additional estimated direct medical costs and imaging delays that increase with reaction severity. Our findings help quantify how these adverse events increase direct and indirect estimated direct medical costs and negatively affect Radiology workflow; providing decision makers with important economic and operational context.

articles.title: Geometry-Guided Graph Encoding Network (G3e-Net) for Patient-Specific Prediction of Vascular Haemodynamics.
articles.abstract: Patient-specific haemodynamic assessment is essential for clarifying vascular pathophysiology and guiding clinical decision-making. While computational fluid dynamics offers high-fidelity flow quantification, its routine clinical use remains limited by the time-consuming iterative solution process required for patient-specific simulations. To tackle these issues, we developed a geometry-guided graph encoding network (G3e-Net), a CFD-supervised image-derived prediction framework that learns anatomically informed representations from CTA-derived vascular geometries. G3e-Net coupled centerline-guided spectral encoding to resolve global topology with multi-scale curvature descriptors capturing local boundary nuances. An attention mechanism then combined these different spatial representations, allowing the network to dynamically balance global connectivity with local geometry in complicated vascular structures. By learning a direct mapping from CTA-derived point clouds to three-dimensional haemodynamic fields, G3e-Net enables rapid functional estimation without requiring volumetric meshing or iterative numerical optimization during inference. Extensive validation on thoracic aortas and carotid arteries from multiple hospitals confirmed that G3e-Net outperformed state-of-the-art baselines, reducing prediction errors for velocity, pressure, and WSS by 10-20%. Notably, inference on high-resolution aortic geometries comprising approximately 200,000 nodes was completed in less than 4 seconds, providing substantial acceleration compared with conventional CFD. These results support the potential of anatomically informed graph representation learning for rapid image-derived haemodynamic analysis and patient-specific functional vascular assessment in thoracic aortic and carotid artery applications.

articles.title: Sex-related differences in baseline neuroimaging, treatment workflow, and outcomes of ischemic stroke following thrombectomy: data from an inverse propensity score weighted analysis.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: We investigated sex differences in baseline neuroimaging, treatment workflow, and outcomes among ischemic stroke patients undergoing endovascular treatment (EVT) within 24 h from last known well. METHODS: Consecutive stroke patients who underwent a multimodal CT study protocol, EVT, and non-contrast CT follow-up imaging at 24 h were analyzed. We compared clinical and safety outcomes between males and females who received EVT in both the original population and a Propensity Score-balanced set. We performed univariable analyses to identify baseline neuroimaging, treatment workflow, and outcomes that differed between sexes. We used multivariable logistic regression to assess whether sex was associated with outcomes after adjusting for covariates. RESULTS: Among 615 patients included in the analysis, 318 (51.7%) were female. Compared to females, males were younger (p <0.001), more independent before stroke (p <0.001), had a lower prevalence of atrial fibrillation (p < 0.001), and had lower internal carotid artery occlusion (p < 0.013). Compared to male, females had lower total hypoperfused tissue (109.3 mL [IQR=66.4-151.3] vs. 86.3 mL [IQR=43.4-132.3]; p<0.001), lower penumbra volumes (78.1 mL [IQR=43.9-114.8] vs. 47.7 mL [IQR=24.6-76.6], p<0.001), lower mismatch ratio (2.63 [IQR=1.86-4.49] vs. 3.67 [IQR=2.27-6.53]; p<0.001), and lower hypoperfusion intensity ratio (0.30 [IQR=0.18-0.50] vs. 0.38 [IQR=0.22-0.50]; p<0.001). In multivariable logistic regression analysis, sex was not an independent predictor of good clinical outcomes after EVT, although females died less than males and had a lower incidence of hemorrhagic transformation. CONCLUSION: In our cohort of acute ischemic stroke treated with EVT, females showed an overall better perfusion profile at baseline compared to males, suggesting they may be slow progressors; however, this did not translate into better clinical outcomes. More data are needed to clarify the relationship between neuroimaging and sex, as well as the influence of other clinical factors on outcomes among patients undergoing EVT.

articles.title: Pediatric chronological age estimation from pelvic radiographs using deep learning: a multicenter retrospective study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Pelvic bones exhibit multiple secondary ossification centers during maturation, enabling automated age estimation. This study investigated whether a deep learning model could estimate chronological age from pelvic radiographs across the full pediatric age range. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included pelvic radiographs from two hospitals for model development, from patients aged between 0 and 18 years. A DenseNet161 model was trained to classify age into 19 1-year interval categories using chronological age as a reference standard and conditional ordinal regression (CORN) loss. External validation was conducted using two independent cohorts, including 541 radiographs from a different department of the same hospital and 203 from an external hospital. External validation was performed on 744 radiographs from two independent cohorts. Model performance was evaluated using the accuracy of predictions within 1 year of the chronological age (ACC@dist = 1) and the mean absolute error (MAE). RESULTS: A total of 3972 radiographs (median age, 2.5 years; interquartile range, 0-8 years; 2463 males) were included in model development. On the internal test set, the model achieved an MAE of 0.394 years (girls: 0.360; boys: 0.419) and an ACC@dist = 1 of 0.937 (girls: 0.944; boys: 0.931). On the external test sets, the corresponding values were 0.513 years (girls, 0.628; boys, 0.455) and 0.927 (girls, 0.896; boys, 0.943), respectively. CONCLUSION: Automated age estimation in children is feasible from pelvic radiography using a deep neural network. KEY POINTS: Question Pelvic radiographs are commonly obtained in children, yet their potential for automated chronological age estimation across the full pediatric age range remains unexplored. Findings A deep learning model estimated chronological age from pelvic radiographs with a mean absolute error of 0.394 and 0.513 years on internal and external test sets, respectively. Clinical relevance Deep learning-based chronological age estimation from pelvic radiographs is feasible across the full pediatric age range. This approach allows clinically relevant skeletal maturation data to be extracted from imaging already acquired for other indications.

articles.title: Influence of virtual dynamic contrast enhanced breast MRI on lesion size, BI-RADS scores and reader confidence.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Breast MRI routinely uses gadolinium-based contrast agents (GBCAs) for dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) imaging. However, GBCA administration entails periprocedural effort and environmental impact, prompting exploration of contrast-agent-free approaches. Deep learning-based virtual DCE (vDCE) offers a potential solution. This study evaluated vDCE against multiparametric DCE protocols, focusing on BI-RADS, background parenchymal enhancement (BPE), and lesion size. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This IRB-approved retrospective study included 592 3 T examinations divided into training, validation, and test sets. A 2D U-Net generated vDCE series from unenhanced T1-weighted, T2-weighted, and diffusion-weighted acquisitions. Two board-certified radiologists evaluated vDCE and DCE examinations using a BI-RADS-adapted reading protocol. Diagnostic and ordinal outcomes were compared using McNemar and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Bonferroni correction. RESULTS: Mean BI-RADS-based diagnostic accuracy was 76% for vDCE and 77% for DCE. Mean sensitivity was 92% vs 96%, and mean specificity was 65% vs 64%, respectively, without significant differences (both readers, p = 1.0). The mean paired lesion-size difference (DCE minus vDCE) was -2.2 mm in the holdout test set and 0.5 mm in the secondary test set. BPE (R1 p = 1.0; R2 p = 1.0) and artefact ratings (R1 p = 1.0; R2 p = 1.0) did not differ significantly. Reader confidence was high for both protocols, although lower for vDCE for one reader (p = 0.072). CONCLUSION: vDCE showed four-percentage-point lower mean sensitivity and small, cohort-dependent lesion-size biases relative to GBCA-enhanced imaging. Further research is warranted to determine its potential role as a contrast-agent-free approach for selected breast imaging indications. KEY POINTS: Question Breast MRI relies on GBCAs, creating procedural and environmental burdens, while clinically validated contrast-agent-free approaches for BI-RADS-based assessment remain unavailable. Findings Virtual DCE MRI showed lower sensitivity than standard DCE, no significant difference in BPE, but more variable reader confidence and lesion size presentation. Clinical relevance Virtual DCE breast MRI currently demonstrates limited diagnostic performance and requires further optimisation, while additional clinical validation studies are needed to determine its potential as a non-contrast alternative.

articles.title: Ultrasound-guided percutaneous catheter drainage of deep neck space abscesses: outcomes and predictors of treatment failure.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Clinical evidence supporting ultrasound-guided percutaneous catheter drainage (US-PCD) as a first-line treatment for deep neck space abscesses (DNSAs) remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the outcomes of US-PCD as initial management for DNSAs and to identify factors associated with treatment efficacy. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort study included patients with DNSAs who underwent US-PCD as a first-line treatment at four tertiary hospitals in China between 2015 and 2022. All patients were hemodynamically stable and had a stable airway, with preprocedural contrast-enhanced CT/MRI confirming no extensive mediastinal involvement beyond the anterosuperior compartment. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were used to identify preprocedural predictors of US-PCD efficacy. RESULTS: US-PCD was performed in 117 patients. The procedure was technically accessible in 116 (98%) patients, among whom 12 (10%) had descending mediastinitis confined to the anterosuperior mediastinum. No procedure-related major complications occurred. Drainage success was achieved in 98 patients (84%). Among the 18 patients (16%) in whom US-PCD failed, three (3%) died and the remaining 15 (13%) required open surgical drainage. Multiple septations and leukocyte count were significant in univariate but not multivariable analysis. The only independent predictor of drainage failure was the presence of serious associated events-a composite variable including descending mediastinitis, sepsis, airway compromise, and vascular thrombosis (OR = 5.7, 95% CI: 1.9-17.4, p = 0.002). CONCLUSION: Ultrasound-guided percutaneous catheter drainage represents an effective minimally invasive first-line option for selected patients with deep neck space abscesses; however, open surgery should be prioritized when serious associated events are present. KEY POINTS: Question For deep neck space abscesses (DNSAs), ultrasound-guided percutaneous drainage (US-PCD) is a common surgical alternative, but its outcomes and predictors as a first-line treatment remain unclear. Findings US-PCD was effective as a first-line treatment for selected DNSAs. Only serious associated events-mediastinitis, sepsis, airway compromise, and thrombosis-independently predicted drainage failure. Clinical relevance US-PCD may be considered a first-line minimally invasive option for hemodynamically and airway-stable DNSA patients, even with anterosuperior mediastinal extension. Surgical drainage remains prioritized for cases with serious associated events to achieve rapid infection control.

articles.title: Imaging findings of sacroiliac joint degeneration are prevalent in asymptomatic adults: a systemic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The purpose of this study is to determine the prevalence of imaging findings of sacroiliac joint (SIJ) degeneration in asymptomatic adults. MATERIALS AND METHODS: All studies reporting the prevalence of cross-sectional imaging findings of SIJ degeneration in asymptomatic adults through May 2026 were included. Pooled prevalence and 95% confidence intervals were calculated using a random-effects model. Heterogeneity was assessed with I2 and Cochran's Q. Age and sex subgroup analyses were performed. RESULTS: Seventeen studies (3873 patients) were included. Any feature of degeneration was observed in 71.1% of patients (95% CI [25.8, 94.6]) with significant heterogeneity among studies (I2 = 96%, p < .01). Osteophyte formation was most prevalent (68.4%; 95% CI [37.5, 88.7], I2 = 92%), followed by joint space narrowing (45.2%; 95% CI [9.8, 86.3], I2 = 99%), subchondral sclerosis (39.1%; 95% CI [11.7, 75.7], I2 = 96%), vacuum phenomenon (14.3%; 95% CI [6.4, 28.7], I2 = 94%), subchondral cyst formation (5.5%; 95% CI [3.0, 9.9], I2 = 59%), erosions (5.0%; 95% CI [2.1, 11.2], I2 = 86%), and joint ankylosis (2.8%; 95% CI [1.2, 6.5], I2 = 66%). There was a correlation between age and osteophytosis, subchondral sclerosis, and vacuum phenomenon. CONCLUSION: Our study reveals a high prevalence of imaging findings related to SIJ degeneration in asymptomatic adults, which may have a connection with age in several findings. These findings emphasize the importance of correlating imaging with clinical symptoms and physical examination findings in the evaluation of low back pain. Findings should be interpreted with caution because confidence intervals were wide and between-study heterogeneity was high, reflecting differences in imaging modality, lesion definitions, and patient categorization.

articles.title: MRI and proton MR spectroscopy in neonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy: a comprehensive imaging review.
articles.abstract: Neonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) remains a leading cause of neonatal mortality and long-term neurodevelopmental disability. Although cranial ultrasound is widely used as a bedside screening tool, brain MRI has become central to diagnosis, injury pattern classification, timing estimation, and outcome prediction. Furthermore, proton MR spectroscopy (1H-MRS) provides complementary metabolic biomarkers that enhance prognostication. This review focuses on MRI and 1H-MRS in neonatal encephalopathy due to hypoxic-ischemic injury, addressing both term and preterm infants. The pathophysiologic determinants of injury distribution are summarized, the optimal timing of imaging and diffusion evolution is discussed, and practical acquisition protocols including recommended sequences and 1H-MRS parameters are proposed. Key MRI phenotypes in term infants-basal ganglia-thalamus injury, watershed/parasagittal cortical-subcortical injury, and global or near-total injury patterns are reviewed with attention to common pitfalls such as diffusion pseudonormalization and evolving T1/T2 signal changes. For preterm infants, this review highlights distinctive vulnerabilities of the germinal matrix and periventricular white matter, emphasizing the spectrum from punctate white matter injury (WMI) to cystic periventricular leukomalacia (PVL). For 1H-MRS, voxel selection, echo time considerations, and interpretation of lactate, N-acetylaspartate (NAA), choline, creatine, and myo-inositol are detailed. Evidence suggests that deep gray matter lactate/NAA or NAA-based metrics serve as reliable and robust outcome biomarkers. Emerging directions including arterial spin labeling (ASL) perfusion are also discussed.

articles.title: A Survey of Computational Color Constancy: Approaches and Emerging Applications in Medical Imaging.
articles.abstract: As the evening sets in and natural light fades to artificial light, it is remarkable how the colors around us still appear nearly the same. This phenomenon, known as color constancy, allows us to perceive relatively stable colors even as lighting conditions change. In the field of computer vision, replicating this human ability is the key to performing tasks such as recognizing objects and understanding scenes. This review examines two main approaches to tackle the challenge of computational color constancy: traditional static methods that rely on a set of assumptions about lighting and scene conditions, and newer learning-based methods that use models trained to estimate lighting directly from images. We look at how these techniques have evolved, from foundational methods like the gray-world assumption, which work within certain limitations, to modern deep learning techniques that can interpret lighting in more dynamic ways. The datasets, metrics, and reported results of the surveyed studies are consolidated into two comparative tables, providing a structured overview of the methods discussed. Together, these comparisons offer a broad perspective on how computational color constancy has developed and where it is headed, with particular emphasis on its applications in medical imaging.

articles.title: Accelerated Motion-Compensated Diffusion-Weighted pCASL Using Subspace Low-Rank Reconstruction for Quantification of BBB Water Exchange and Permeability.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To develop an accelerated motion-compensated diffusion-weighted pseudo-continuous arterial spin labeling (MCDW-pCASL) method using a spatial subspace low-rank reconstruction method for efficient quantification of blood-brain barrier (BBB) water exchange (kw) and permeability (PSw). METHODS: An accelerated multidelay MCDW-pCASL sequence was developed to simultaneously encode intravascular and extravascular diffusion-weighted ASL signals across multiple post-labeling delays (PLDs). A spatial subspace low-rank reconstruction framework was optimized to enable joint estimation of cerebral blood flow (CBF) and BBB water exchange rate and permeability. Fourteen young healthy adults underwent test-retest scans (separated by ∼1 week) at 3 T with both the accelerated MCDW-pCASL (acceleration factor = 3) and a conventional diffusion-prepared (DP) pCASL sequence. Whole-brain, gray-matter, and white-matter CBF and kw values were quantified to assess test-retest repeatability and cross-method agreement. An additional cohort of 30 older adults underwent single-session MCDW and DP scans to evaluate age-related perfusion and BBB kw/PSw differences. Intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) were used to assess reliability and agreement. RESULTS: Accelerated MCDW-pCASL demonstrated excellent agreement with DP-pCASL for CBF (ICC = 0.89) and fair agreement for kw (ICC = 0.56). Test-retest repeatability of MCDW-pCASL was good for CBF, BBB, kw, and PSw (ICC ≈ 0.6). Across both sequences, younger subjects exhibited significantly higher CBF and kw compared with older adults. CONCLUSION: Incorporating a spatial low-rank subspace reconstruction enables accelerated MCDW-pCASL acquisition with reliable simultaneous quantification of CBF, BBB kw, and PSw. Clinical applications of this method for assessing perfusion and BBB function are warranted.

articles.title: Inertial Navigation Assisted Motion Correction for Brain MRI.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To assess the utility of inertial sensors for estimating parameters describing rigid body motion of the head, and to reduce motion related artifact through a hybrid prospective steering of the rotation via the sensor and retrospective realignment of translation via the MRI data. THEORY AND METHODS: Inertial sensors are widely used for Earth navigation problems. However, drift accumulation from integrating noisy signals makes them impractical for MRI motion correction at millimeter resolution over minute-long scans. Prior work has shown that the MRI system's  B 0   and gravity are approximately orthogonal and can be exploited as reference vectors for 3-DOF orientation estimation. We introduce a hybrid inertial measurement-based method, which uses these fields to estimate 3-DOF orientation directly, without integration, thereby eliminating random walk. The remaining 3-DOF translation is recovered via phase correlation from the MRI data. We validate the efficacy of this hybrid method retrospectively using a 3D radial koosh-ball sequence and prospectively using 2D EPI time-series acquisition during volunteer motions. RESULTS: IMU-based orientation estimation followed by phase correlation achieved a mean accuracy of 0.6° and 0.4 pixels across all experiments. Image quality improved when motion correction was applied in all volunteer scans for both retrospective and prospective correction cases. CONCLUSION: The proposed method measured head motion in the MRI scanner with high accuracy at unprecedented sampling rates and enabled both retrospective and prospective correction, improving image quality by aligning k-space data and reducing motion artifacts.

articles.title: Bilateral Breast Gradient Insert Prototype for Strong Diffusion Encoding at 3 T.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Diffusion MRI has shown promise for breast cancer screening, lesion characterization, and treatment response monitoring without contrast agents, but further translation is constrained by the gradient performance of conventional systems. The aim of this work is to develop a single-axis high-performance bilateral plug-and-play breast gradient insert to enable strong-gradient diffusion MRI. METHODS: An in-house breast gradient insert and bed-tabletop was constructed entirely from commercially available materials, providing a cost-effective solution compatible with existing MRI systems. Its wiring pattern was optimized for torque and force balancing, power dissipation, and target field performance. Evaluation included gradient field characterization, peripheral nerve stimulation simulation verification, and temperature and eddy current assessment. The setup was used for imaging of a diffusion phantom based on soy lecithin across a range of b values. RESULTS: Gradient efficiency ranged from 0.61 to 2.8 mT/m/A, enabling diffusion MRI using local strengths up to 420 mT/m (150 A). No peripheral nerve stimulation was observed during tests on five healthy volunteers. Eddy currents were successfully characterized, revealing a linear first order component with an amplitude of 0.03% of the applied gradient field. Imaging experiments demonstrated the feasibility of acquiring b = 10 000 s/mm2 volumes with a TE of 78 ms, compared with 161 ms when using the scanner gradients (40 mT/m). CONCLUSION: This work demonstrates a dedicated bilateral breast gradient insert for safe and feasible strong-gradient breast diffusion MRI and represents a first step toward dedicated hardware for breast cancer detection and characterization without contrast agents.

articles.title: Multiecho Imaging With Intrinsic Fat Suppression.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To investigate a modification of the RARE(TSE,FSE)-method for chemical shift selective imaging without additional chemical shift selective preparation pulses at high fields. METHODS: The method is based on a standard TSE-sequence, where the excitation pulse is displaced by a time shift of dTE. dTE is set such that fat signal experiences a phase shift by 90° with respect to on resonance spins. As a result, the signal from fat will experience the ensuing echo train as a rapidly decaying CP-echo train, whereas water will show the beneficial CPMG-conditions. RESULTS: Results on human volunteers demonstrate the efficient fat suppression of the TE-shifting especially for T2-weighted imaging of the head at 3 and 5 T. The time shift is sufficiently small to keep the T2-contrast constant. CONCLUSION: TE-shifted TSE has demonstrated to be an efficient method for fat suppression without the need of additional fat suppression pulses. The fat suppression scheme is largely independent of the actual flip angles used and thus very robust against B1-inhomogeneities. The method is sensitive to B0-inhomogeneities, which limits its usefulness outside of the head.

articles.title: Multistage Preclinical Evaluation of MRI-Guided Stenting for Coarctation of the Aorta using in vitro and Porcine Models.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: This study evaluated the technical and procedural feasibility of MRI-guided stent implantation for CoA using a structured multistage preclinical evaluation protocol. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A commercially available MR Conditional guidewire and dedicated research prototypes comprising nitinol stents, delivery systems, and balloon catheters were assessed in a three-stage protocol. Device visibility was evaluated in a standardized water phantom at 1.5 T and 3.0 T. In a polymer-based CoA vessel phantom, 10 stent implantations were performed by novices (n = 6) and experts (n = 4), with four separate expert-led balloon dilatations. MRI-guided stent implantation was subsequently performed in five porcine models. RESULTS: All devices were visible at both field strengths, with lateral artifact widths of 5.3-7.8 mm for the guidewire, 20.9-38.5 mm for the stent delivery system, 13.1-19.9 mm for the expanded stents, and 17.4-30.5 mm for the balloon catheter. Phantom stenting duration was 10.2 ± 7.2 mins for novices and 6.2 ± 2.7 mins for experts. MRI-guided stent implantation was successfully performed in all five animals, with a mean duration of 13.6 ± 7.5 mins. In one animal, balloon post-dilatation was additionally performed as a procedural proof of concept. CONCLUSION: MRI-guided stent implantation for CoA is feasible within a structured multistage preclinical evaluation protocol and supports further clinical translation of radiation-free endovascular treatment.

articles.title: MRI Features in Children with Pituitary Stalk Interruption Syndrome: Associations with Hormonal Phenotype and Intracranial Anomalies.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Pituitary stalk interruption syndrome (PSIS) is a rare congenital disorder with variable endocrine and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) phenotypes, and the relationship between MRI features, hormonal phenotype, and associated intracranial anomalies remains incompletely understood. This study evaluated MRI features associated with hormonal phenotype and intracranial anomalies in pediatric PSIS. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 51 pediatric patients with biochemically confirmed pituitary hormone deficiency and MRI findings of PSIS. Pituitary stalk morphology was classified as absent, interrupted, or thin. Anterior pituitary volume was assessed by two- and three-dimensional methods, and two-dimensional volumes were converted to age- and sex-specific z-scores. We analyzed associations between MRI findings, hormonal phenotype, and intracranial anomalies using univariable and multivariable methods. RESULTS: Growth hormone deficiency was present in 49 patients (96.1%) and multiple pituitary hormone deficiency (MPHD) in 23 (45.1%). Intracranial anomalies were detected in 31 patients (60.8%), most commonly corpus callosum dysgenesis. MPHD was more frequent with an absent stalk (18/23, 78.3%) than with an interrupted (3/8, 37.5%) or thin stalk (2/20, 10.0%) (p < 0.001), and intracranial anomalies followed the same gradient (p < 0.001). After adjustment for age and intracranial anomalies, absent or interrupted stalk morphology remained independently associated with MPHD (odds ratio 16.8, 95% confidence interval 2.2-130.1; p = 0.007), driven primarily by the absent-stalk group. Neither two- nor three-dimensional anterior pituitary volume nor volume z-scores differed significantly between the isolated deficiency and MPHD groups; sella morphology also showed no significant association with hormonal phenotype. CONCLUSION: Pituitary stalk morphology, particularly an absent stalk, showed the strongest association with hormonal phenotype and intracranial anomalies in pediatric PSIS.

articles.title: A Hybrid Human-AI Workflow for Ultrasound Report Quality Control: A Multicenter Performance and Efficiency Evaluation.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated a hybrid human-AI workflow for ultrasound report quality assurance using multicenter retrospective data. MATERIALS AND METHODS: 786 anonymized ultrasound reports covering 22 examination categories were collected from four hospitals. Reports containing naturally occurring or implanted errors were matched across arms. GPT-4o and DeepSeek-v3 performed initial screening before review by six human reviewers (HRs). HR with blinded expert over-reading (HR-ex) served as control. Accuracy, false-positive (FP) and false-negative (FN) rates, and review time were compared. Supplementary validation compared HR and DeepSeek-assisted review using 1680 consecutive reports without implanted errors. RESULTS: Hybrid workflow (HYB) accuracy was comparable to HR (4o-HYB 80.2%, v3-HYB 82.5%, HR 82.3%) but lower than HR-ex (87.3%). Both HYBs showed higher FN rates than HR-ex (4o-HYB 34.2% and v3-HYB 27.3% vs HR-ex 16.9%, both p < 0.001). Severity assessment did not indicate preferential omission of clinically significant errors. Human verification reduced LLM-generated FNs and FPs. Median review time decreased substantially from 51.0 s (HR-ex) to 11.0 s (4o-HYB) and 12.0 s (v3-HYB). In supplementary validation (error prevalence, 9.6%), v3.2-HYB and HR showed FN rates of 22.6% and 24.3%, FP rates of 7.7% and 10.0%, and median review times of 15.4 and 24.3 s, respectively. CONCLUSION: The LLM-assisted HYB achieved accuracy comparable to single-physician review while substantially reducing audit time. These findings require prospective real-world validation before routine clinical implementation.

articles.title: Hyperdense Renal Lesion Characterization on Three DECT Technologies: Can Iodine Quantification Differentiate Hyperattenuating Renal Cysts From Papillary Renal Cell Cancers?
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the performance of dual-energy computed tomography (DECT) in differentiation of hyperattenuating renal cysts (HCs) from papillary renal cell cancers (pRCCs) on three different DECT technologies (dual-source [dsDECT], rapid kVp-switching [rsDECT], and dual-layer detector-based [dlDECT]). MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this institutional review board-approved retrospective study, we included 85 patients with a total of 108 incidental hyperdense renal lesions detected on contrast-enhanced DECT scans (dsDECT, n = 41; rsDECT, n = 42; and dlDECT, n = 25). The study cohort included HCs (n = 73) and pRCCs (n = 35). Final confirmation was obtained with histopathology for pRCCs and with magnetic resonance imaging within 6 months of the DECT for HCs. Quantitative iodine evaluation was performed with iodine concentration (IC) measured within the lesion and the abdominal aorta. Normalized IC (NIC) was generated for each lesion by normalizing the lesion IC to the aortic IC. RESULTS: Both IC and NIC measurements yielded significant differences between HCs and pRCCs for the dsDECT and rsDECT techniques (P < 0.001) but not for the dlDECT (P > 0.05). Cutoff values with 100% sensitivity for pRCC detection were 0.30 and 0.60 mg/mL for dsDECT and rsDECT, respectively. Normalization to the abdominal aorta allowed creation of a uniform cutoff on both technologies, with an NIC value of 0.09 allowing 100% sensitivity for each. CONCLUSION: Significant intertechnique differences exist for the differentiation of HCs from pRCCs. Normalization of IC to the aorta provides a uniform cutoff for differentiation of these lesions on dsDECT and rsDECT.

articles.title: Differential Cerebral Perfusion Patterns Across Migraine Phenotypes: An Exploratory ASL MRI Study.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: This study aims to characterize cerebral blood flow (CBF) alterations across migraine phenotypes and determine whether perfusion measures provide additional information for phenotype differentiation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The final cohort comprised 143 patients with migraine and 49 healthy controls who underwent three-dimensional pseudo-continuous arterial spin labeling (ASL) MRI. Voxel-wise analyses of normalized CBF (nCBF) were performed to identify phenotype-related perfusion alterations. Sensitivity analyses repeated the voxel-wise comparisons with phenotype-appropriate clinical covariates. Exploratory correlation analyses examined associations between regional perfusion and clinical characteristics. Logistic regression was further used to assess whether perfusion measures provided additional information for differentiating migraine with aura (MA) from migraine without aura (MO). RESULTS: Compared with healthy controls, migraine patients with depressive symptoms showed reduced nCBF in a right hippocampus-parahippocampal cluster (Cluster 1) in the primary voxel-wise analysis; however, this finding did not survive additional adjustment for sleep quality. Lower Cluster 1 nCBF was associated with greater headache frequency. Compared with MO, patients with MA showed increased nCBF in a right cerebellar-occipitotemporal cluster peaking in the right cerebellar Crus I (Cluster 2), and this difference remained significant after additional adjustment for sleep quality, medication-overuse headache status, and preventive medication exposure. Within the MA group, higher Cluster 2 nCBF was associated with greater headache intensity. In exploratory logistic regression analysis, the combined clinical-imaging model showed a higher apparent area under the curve (AUC) than the clinical model alone. CONCLUSION: Clinically relevant migraine phenotypes showed distinct patterns of regional cerebral perfusion. These findings highlight the importance of considering clinical heterogeneity in migraine neuroimaging and suggest that ASL-derived perfusion measures may provide complementary biological information for phenotype characterization, particularly with respect to aura status.

articles.title: Precise modeling of task-related sensorimotor activation based on simultaneous surface electromyography.
articles.abstract: The aim of this study was to evaluate the relationship between motor control of ankle movements and actual motor performance using simultaneous functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and surface electromyography (EMG) in healthy individuals. Twenty participants performed dorsi-/plantarflexion of the ankle (Ankle) and gait imagery in a block design during fMRI. First-level models consisting of task regressors included either orthogonalized accelerometry (Acc) from the foot, EMG from the tibialis anterior, EMG with Acc, EMG split across conditions, or none. Each model was additionally evaluated either by default with or without a temporal derivative (TD) of the ankle movement task regressor. Voxel-wise and post-hoc region-of-interest (ROI) analyses revealed that both Acc and EMG explained fMRI signal in the primary sensorimotor cortices, while EMG was additionally associated with activation in the cerebellar vermis and the secondary somatosensory cortex. The two latter findings were, however, neither reproduced when separating the signal fluctuations during rest and gait imagery nor reflected in pairwise comparisons. Leaving out the TD reduced each model's performance by increasing unexplained variance, but resulted in more signal being explained by the EMG or Acc in the cerebellum, reflecting that it preferentially exhibited brief signal changes during transitions between conditions. Taken together, both EMG and Acc enabled capturing specific brain activity related to the movement variability; however, including the TD may significantly affect the ability to detect EMG- or Acc-related signal in regions with transient fMRI responses sensitive to changes in movement context, such as the cerebellum.

articles.title: Interplay of action-based prediction and top-down attention: EEG evidence for joint modulation of late perceptual processing.
articles.abstract: Voluntary action shapes our perception through sensory predictions of its consequences. These predictions are thought to inhibit perceptual processing of predicted outcomes, leading to sensory attenuation. However, some studies have reported findings that contrast with this effect, suggesting that the influence of predictions may reflect, or interact with, attentional processes. Here, we investigated the interplay of action-based prediction and top-down attention on early and late perceptual processing, with prediction and attention referring to the likelihood of a sensory event and its behavioral relevance, respectively. Electroencephalography (EEG) was recorded while participants viewed two sequential gratings. The orientation of the first was either predicted and self-generated or unpredicted and externally generated. Participants judged the tilt direction of the second grating relative to the first but responded only when the grating appeared in a task-relevant color. EEG analyses revealed no modulation of early visual potentials (N1a), but modulations at later processing stages. Specifically, the P3b exhibited reduced amplitude for predicted compared to unpredicted stimuli, but only when they were task-relevant, whereas task-relevance enhanced the P3b only for unpredicted stimuli. Interestingly, multivariate pattern analysis showed significant temporal clusters for decoding the grating's orientation exclusively for predicted and task-relevant stimuli, although decoding performance did not significantly differ between conditions. Furthermore, predicted and task-relevant stimuli elicited faster behavioral responses, with prediction-related P3b latency differences correlating with reaction-time differences. Overall, converging findings from the P3b, multivariate, time-frequency and behavioral analyses provide suggestive evidence that top-down attention and action-based prediction may jointly facilitate late perceptual and decision-related processing.

articles.title: 5.0-T magnetic resonance imaging and contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance angiography for the evaluation of juvenile idiopathic arthritis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is the most sensitive non-invasive method for assessing joint lesions in juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA), but conventional protocols cannot simultaneously depict synovial inflammation and the associated vascular changes. OBJECTIVE: To assess changes in the "synovium-vascular axis" of the hand in children with JIA using 5.0-T MRI and contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance angiography (CE-MRA). MATERIALS AND METHODS: Twenty children with JIA and 10 age- and sex-matched healthy controls underwent hand 5.0-T MRI, including contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging and CE-MRA. The maximum synovial thickness, enhancement rate, bone marrow edema score, palmar digital artery diameter ratios, palmar arch integrity, distal microcirculation score, and vascular tortuosity were quantified. Correlations with the Juvenile Arthritis Disease Activity Score-27 (JADAS-27), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), and C-reactive protein (CRP) were analyzed. RESULTS: Compared with controls, the JIA group showed higher maximum synovial thickness (5.19±2.35 mm vs. 0.83±0.24 mm, P<0.001), enhancement rate (0.44±0.20 vs. 0.20±0.14, P=0.002), bone marrow edema score (median 7.50 vs. 0, P<0.001), and vascular tortuosity (2.0 vs. 0, P<0.001), but lower common palmar digital artery diameter ratio (0.690 vs. 1.000, P<0.001) and microcirculation score (1.0 vs. 3.0, P<0.001). The bone marrow edema score (r=0.674, P=0.001), maximum synovial thickness (r=0.581, P=0.007), and enhancement rate (r=0.634, P=0.003) correlated positively with JADAS-27, and the bone marrow edema score was independently associated with ln(JADAS-27) (standardized β=0.677, P=0.005). CONCLUSION: Combined 5.0-T MRI and CE-MRA revealed a distinct pattern of synovial inflammation, arterial narrowing, and impaired distal microcirculatory perfusion in children with JIA. CE-MRA-derived vascular parameters are candidate exploratory imaging markers requiring validation in larger multicenter cohorts.

articles.title: MR elastography and perfusion MRI characterize distinct biomechanical and vascular features of meningiomas.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To determine whether MR elastography (MRE) and dynamic susceptibility contrast (DSC) perfusion MRI provide overlapping or complementary information in meningiomas using anatomically matched regions of interest (ROIs). METHODS: Fifty-five patients with histopathologically confirmed meningiomas who underwent preoperative 3-T MRE and DSC perfusion MRI were retrospectively analyzed. MRE-derived stiffness and relative cerebral blood volume (rCBV) were evaluated in whole-tumor, MRE-defined high-stiffness (local), and non-focal ROIs. Regional differences, histological subtype associations, stiffness-perfusion correlations, and the influence of calcification were assessed. RESULTS: MRE-derived stiffness was higher in the local than non-focal ROI (p < 0.001), whereas rCBV did not differ significantly (p = 0.274). MRE-derived stiffness and rCBV were not significantly correlated in the local, whole-tumor, or non-focal ROIs (ρ = 0.085-0.182; all p ≥ 0.183). Fibroblastic meningiomas showed lower local rCBV than meningothelial meningiomas (median, 4.01 vs. 9.87; p = 0.004), whereas MRE-derived stiffness did not differ significantly among histological subtypes (local p = 0.748). In the fibroblastic-meningothelial comparison, the stiffness effect size was small with a confidence interval spanning zero (r = - 0.126; 95% bootstrap CI, - 0.51 to 0.29). SWI-detected calcification was associated with lower rCBV but not MRE-derived stiffness. CONCLUSION: Perfusion did not differ significantly between MRE-defined high-stiffness and non-focal regions, and no significant stiffness-rCBV association was detected across ROI types. Perfusion MRI nevertheless demonstrated histological subtype-related differences not observed with MRE-derived stiffness, suggesting that the two modalities provide different, potentially complementary information about meningioma biomechanical and vascular features.

articles.title: Neuroimaging findings in hyperammonemic encephalopathy associated with sepsis-induced liver injury: a pilot case series.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hyperammonemic encephalopathy (HE) is a severe complication of sepsis-induced liver injury (SILI), often associated with sepsis. However, its neuroimaging manifestations remain poorly understood. The aim of this pilot case series is to describe the brain MRI findings in patients with sepsis and HE. METHODS: We analysed brain MRI data from 15 consecutive patients with sepsis and clinically confirmed HE. Assessment of cerebral changes was performed using a standard MRI protocol. The following parameters were evaluated during the analysis: localization and signal intensity characteristics of the lesions on MRI, presence or absence of diffusion restriction, presence magnetic susceptibility artifacts, and reversibility on follow‑up were evaluated descriptively. No control group was included. RESULTS: Pathological changes were observed in all 15 patients. Symmetrical involvement of the insular cortex and cingulate gyrus was the most frequent pattern (13/15, 86.7%), followed by basal ganglia lesions (1/15) and cortico‑subcortical hemispheric lesions (1/15). All lesions were hyperintense on T2‑WI and FLAIR, with diffusion restriction on DWI suggestive of cytotoxic oedema. Follow-up MRI was performed in all patients after treatment adjustment and renal replacement therapy, demonstrating marked regression of all noted changes, concurrent with normalization of serum ammonia, transaminases, lactate and sepsis markers.

articles.title: A multi-stage multimodal learning model for functional outcomes prediction in acute ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: Predicting functional outcomes in acute ischemic stroke (AIS) patients after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) remains challenging due to the complex and dynamic nature of disease progression. Existing methods typically rely on single-stage imaging or limited multimodal fusion, failing to fully capture disease progression and cross-modal complementarity. To address this issue, we propose a multimodal deep learning framework that integrates multi-stage imaging and clinical notes for 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) prediction. The proposed model leverages a shared foundation model with Low-Rank Adaptation to encode pre- and post-treatment images. It further introduces a shared feature extraction module and a stage-specific feature extraction module to disentangle shared and stage-specific representations, enabling effective modeling of disease progression across stages. In addition, a bidirectional cross-attention module is employed to enhance semantic alignment between imaging features and clinical notes. Experiments on multi-stage NCCT and MRI datasets demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms single-modality baselines, achieving AUCs of 0.9147 and 0.9479, respectively. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of both the multi-stage interaction design and the multimodal fusion strategy. These results suggest that integrating pre- and post-treatment imaging with clinical notes can improve prognostic performance, providing a practical solution for individualized outcome prediction in AIS patients following EVT.

articles.title: Improving the fairness and robustness of deep learning classification models through bias mitigation and post hoc calibration.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: The goal of this study was to enhance the fairness and clinical applicability of deep learning models for classifying Alzheimer's disease from structural MRI scans. To achieve this, we addressed two key challenges: age-related bias and unreliable probability estimates. Specifically, we investigated in-processing debiasing strategies to achieve age-invariant predictions while preserving diagnostic accuracy. We also systematically evaluated post hoc calibration methods to improve the reliability, interpretability, and clinical usefulness of predicted probabilities across diverse patient populations. METHODS: Structural MRI data from three independent cohorts (ADNI, AIBL, and DELCODE) were preprocessed using a standardized pipeline. Age-related bias was addressed using two in-processing strategies, adversarial training (CF-Net) and GLM-based feature residualization (PMDN), implemented in a shared 3D convolutional neural network (CNN) framework. Additionally, post hoc calibration was performed using four regression methods: logistic, probit, isotonic, and Bayesian binning. We evaluated model performance, fairness, and calibration using classification as well as calibration-specific metrics. RESULTS: PMDN achieved the best overall performance, with higher balanced accuracy (0.71) and improved calibration (Brier ≈ 0.22), showing substantially reduced variability compared to baseline and CF-Net. PMDN effectively removed age-related bias, achieving near-zero age prediction correlation; CF-Net, however, showed only partial and unstable debiasing. Post hoc calibration further improved probability reliability, with nonparametric methods (isotonic regression and Bayesian binning) yielding the lowest calibration errors (MCE ≈ 0.21-0.24). CONCLUSION: This study shows that, although deep learning models achieve similar classification performance, they differ significantly in terms of calibration, stability, and fairness. PMDN provides more consistent and effective age bias mitigation than the CF-Net approach, particularly in clinically relevant subgroups. Post hoc calibration improves probability reliability further, with nonparametric methods achieving the best calibration.
articles.journal: Int J Comput Assist Radiol Surg

articles.title: Comparison of PMAneo and RAPID in acute ischemic stroke: agreement in CT perfusion analysis and DEFUSE 3 imaging eligibility.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Automated computed tomography perfusion (CTP) analysis plays a key role in triaging acute ischemic stroke (AIS). This study aimed to evaluate the agreement of PMAneo compared with RAPID in a multicenter setting. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 99 patients with anterior circulation AIS from three stroke centers using four different CT scanners. CTP data were processed using both PMAneo and RAPID. Volumetric agreement for ischemic core volume and Tmax > 6 s volume was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) and Bland-Altman analysis. Multivariable regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with volume discrepancies. EVT imaging eligibility was evaluated according to the DEFUSE 3 criteria (ischemic core volume < 70 mL, mismatch ratio ≥ 1.8, and absolute mismatch volume ≥ 15 mL), using RAPID as the comparator. RESULTS: Ischemic core volumes showed excellent agreement between the two platforms (ICC = 0.881, 95% CI 0.827-0.918), and Tmax > 6 s volumes showed good agreement (ICC = 0.761, 95% CI 0.283-0.896), whereas mismatch volumes showed moderate agreement (ICC = 0.661, 95% CI 0.146-0.844). For the ischemic core threshold (< 70 mL), PMAneo demonstrated 100% (95% CI 96-100%) relative sensitivity and 67% (95% CI 38-88%) relative specificity. For the full DEFUSE 3 criteria, the relative sensitivity and specificity were 81% (95% CI 70-89%) and 84% (95% CI 66-95%), respectively. Bland-Altman analysis demonstrated proportional bias, with PMAneo underestimating volumes relative to RAPID as lesion size increased. Basal ganglia involvement and imaging site were significantly associated with these volume differences (p < 0.05). CONCLUSION: PMAneo showed high volumetric agreement and comparable DEFUSE 3 imaging eligibility to RAPID, suggesting it is a reliable alternative for automated CTP analysis. Although proportional bias and potential diagnostic discrepancies were observed in borderline cases near clinically relevant thresholds, PMAneo may facilitate broader access to automated CTP analysis.

articles.title: Photon-counting computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging in rectal cancer: reassessment of normalized iodine concentration and apparent diffusion coefficient in an expanded cohort.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To reassess pretreatment photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT)-derived normalized iodine concentration (NIC) in an expanded rectal-cancer cohort, using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-derived apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) as a within-cohort reference marker for histopathologic treatment response. METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 63 patients with rectal adenocarcinoma who underwent pretreatment pelvic MRI and contrast-enhanced PCCT, followed by neoadjuvant treatment and surgical resection. Dworak tumor regression grades 0-1 were classified as poor response (n = 22) and grades 2-4 as moderate/good response (n = 41). MRI and PCCT were performed a median of 3 days apart (IQR, 1-4.5). The previously reported NIC threshold of ≥ 0.36 was reassessed without re-optimization. Twenty-one of 63 patients overlapped with the preceding pilot cohort; therefore, the present study is an expanded reassessment rather than an independent external validation. RESULTS: Twenty-two patients showed poor response and 41 moderate/good response. ADC interobserver agreement was excellent (ICC, 0.959; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.90-0.98). In the 61 patients with paired numeric NIC measurements from both observers, NIC interobserver agreement was also excellent (ICC, 0.905; bootstrap 95% CI, 0.858-0.936). Mean ADC was lower in poor responders than in moderate/good responders (0.876 ± 0.186 vs. 1.035 ± 0.208 × 10⁻³ mm²/s; p = 0.003; AUC, 0.738; 95% CI, 0.608-0.867). NIC did not differ between groups (median, 0.313 vs. 0.370; p = 0.91; AUC, 0.509; 95% CI, 0.362-0.656). Applying the previously published NIC threshold ≥ 0.36 yielded sensitivity 53.7%, specificity 63.6%, and accuracy 57.1% for Dworak grades 2-4. Adding NIC to ADC did not improve model fit (likelihood-ratio p = 0.601). CONCLUSION: In this exploratory expanded cohort, lower pretreatment ADC was associated with Dworak grades 0-1. Single-phase portal-venous NIC measured with the described two-dimensional ROI approach did not reproduce the high performance reported in the pilot study and showed no evidence of improved model fit beyond ADC in this cohort. These findings require independent prospective validation.

articles.title: Structured MRI reporting for deep pelvic endometriosis: objective report quality and surgeon-perceived clinical utility in a randomized comparative study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To compare structured and free-text MRI reporting in terms of objective report quality and surgeon ratings of perceived clinical utility in suspected deep pelvic endometriosis. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this single-center randomized reader study, 20 radiology residents were assigned to free-text or structured reporting. Five residents became unavailable before report generation and provided no outcome data. The remaining 15 readers completed the same 22 pelvic MRI examinations, generating 330 reports: 154 free-text and 176 structured reports. Reports were compared with an imaging reference standard established by two pelvic radiologists through independent review and consensus adjudication. The primary endpoint was clinically weighted completeness. Secondary endpoints included unweighted completeness, explicit negative discrepancies relative to the expert imaging reference, positive findings unsupported by the expert imaging reference, and reporting time. Objective outcomes were analyzed using mixed-effects models or Poisson generalized estimating equations. In an exploratory paired assessment, two expert gynecologic surgeons evaluated 44 reports, comprising one free-text and one structured report for each MRI examination. RESULTS: Structured reporting was associated with an 8.1%-point increase in completeness compared with free-text reporting (95% CI, 4.1-12.1; p < 0.001) and a 5.6%-point increase in clinically weighted completeness (95% CI, 1.3-10.0; p = 0.011). Reporting time was 4.52 min longer with structured reporting (95% CI, 3.05-5.99; p < 0.001). Structured reporting was also associated with more explicit negative discrepancies relative to the expert imaging reference (rate ratio, 2.94; 95% CI, 1.73-4.98; p < 0.001). These discrepancies were mainly explicit compartment-based negative statements. In the exploratory surgeon assessment, structured reports received higher ratings for perceived completeness, usefulness for clinical decision-making, and adequacy to clinical needs, whereas clarity ratings were similar between formats. CONCLUSION: Structured MRI reporting was associated with higher objective completeness and, in an exploratory assessment, higher surgeon ratings for several dimensions of perceived clinical utility. These findings should be balanced against longer reporting time and more explicit negative discrepancies relative to the expert imaging reference.

articles.title: Radiological lymphoceles and clinically relevant lymphatic complications after retroperitoneal lymph node dissection for testicular cancer: a longitudinal imaging study.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Postoperative lymphoceles are recognized complications of retroperitoneal lymph node dissection (RPLND) for testicular germ cell tumours (TGCT). Previous studies have predominantly reported symptomatic or intervention-requiring lymphoceles, whereas the incidence, temporal evolution, and clinical relevance of lymphoceles on postoperative imaging remain poorly defined. We evaluated radiologically detected lymphoceles and clinically relevant lymphatic complications after post-chemotherapy RPLND (PC-RPLND) using routine serial imaging. METHODS: This retrospective single-centre cohort study included 86 consecutive patients who underwent PC-RPLND under a standardized perioperative management protocol. Postoperative imaging consisted of ultrasound at postoperative day 5-7 and 3-4 weeks, followed by computed tomography at 3 and 12 months. The primary endpoint was the incidence of any imaging-detected lymphocele during follow-up. Secondary endpoints included lymphocele prevalence at each imaging time point, clinically relevant lymphatic complications, postoperative complications, and exploratory factors associated with lymphocele formation. RESULTS: Of 86 included patients, 85 were evaluable for the primary endpoint. Overall, 46 patients (54.1%) had at least one imaging-detected lymphocele during follow-up. Lymphoceles were most frequently detected at discharge (36/84, 42.9%) and decreased over time to 32.8% (19/58) at 3-4 weeks, 31.5% (17/54) at 3 months, and 15.8% (9/57) at 12 months. Clinical follow-up was available for 65 patients. Clinically relevant lymphatic complications occurred in only 3 patients (4.6%), comprising two cases of lymphatic/chylous ascites and one lymphatic fistula associated with a small precaval lymphocele. Among 49 patients with paired 3- and 12-month CT, 10 of 16 lymphoceles present at 3 months had resolved by 12 months, whereas only one was newly detected (exact McNemar p = .012). Exploratory analyses identified no significant associations between imaging-detected lymphocele formation and patient characteristics, tumour-related factors, surgical approach, or extent of lymphadenectomy. CONCLUSIONS: Lymphoceles are frequently detected by routine serial imaging after PC-RPLND but rarely translate into clinically relevant lymphatic morbidity. Radiologically detected lymphoceles should therefore be distinguished from clinically relevant lymphatic complications when interpreting surveillance imaging, counselling patients, and reporting postoperative outcomes after RPLND.

articles.title: Photon counting detector CTA for prostate arterial evaluation during the workup for prostate artery embolization.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate small field of view (FOV) ultra-high spatial resolution pelvic photon-counting detector prostate CT angiograms (UHR PCD CTA) for identifying prostate arterial anatomy and extraprostatic anastomoses in patients undergoing workup for prostate artery embolization (PAE). METHODS: IRB-approved retrospective imaging and electronic medical record review of men who consecutively underwent UHR PCD CTA for PAE workup at our institution from 8/1/2022 to 12/1/2024. UHR PCD CTAs were evaluated by two vascular and interventional radiologists for main and accessory candidate prostatic arteries (PA/s) and anastomoses to penile, bladder, or rectal arteries. A main PA was defined as supplying the central gland and an accessory PA was defined as supplying the peripheral zone. PAs were categorized using the Carnevale classification. In patients who proceeded to PAE, digital subtraction angiograms (DSA) were retrospectively compared with UHR PCD CTA findings. RESULTS: UHR PCD CTA was obtained prior to PAE consultation for 50 men. We evaluated 100 pelvic sides, identifying 180 candidate PAs with a median of 3 candidate PAs per patient (mean, 3.6; range, 2-7). Overall, 56% (101/180) of candidate PAs were main and 44% (79/180) were accessory. Abridged Carnevale classifications: Type 5-21% (38/180). Eight accessory candidate PAs arose from the superior rectal artery. At least one candidate anastomosis arose from 40% (72/180) of candidate PAs. Of 95 total candidate anastomoses, 69 were extraprostatic (30 rectal, 20 bladder, 19 penile) and 26 were intraprostatic collaterals; 56% (53/95) arose from accessory and 44% (42/95) from main candidate PAs. Twenty-eight of 50 (56%) men underwent PAE, during which 72% (74/103) of available candidate PAs were selected, and prostatic supply was confirmed by DSA in 100% (74/74) of selected vessels. CONCLUSION: Small FOV UHR PCD CTA is useful in identifying candidate PA supply, as well as potential extraprostatic anastomoses, providing an arterial roadmap for PAE planning. Candidate PA supply was confirmed by DSA in all selected vessels among patients who proceeded to PAE.

articles.title: Palliative radiotherapy for gastric cancer-related bleeding: a systematic review and meta-analysis of bleeding response and dose-response relationships.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Palliative radiotherapy is commonly used to control bleeding in advanced gastric cancer; however, the optimal dose-fractionation regimen as well as the dose-response relationship remain unclear. We aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of radiotherapy for gastric cancer-related bleeding and its association with dose fractionation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, and Ichushi-Web for studies published between January 2000 and August 2026 on palliative radiotherapy for gastric cancer-related bleeding. The primary endpoint was bleeding response rate. A random-effects meta-analysis was performed to estimate the pooled response rates. Meta-regression and subgroup analyses were conducted to explore dose-response relationships. Meta-regression was performed using study-level median biologically effective dose (BED) values. RESULTS: A total of 31 studies were included. The pooled bleeding response rate was 75.9% (95% confidence interval, 69.7-81.2), with significant heterogeneity (I2 = 67.5%). Egger's test suggested small study effects (P = 0.012). Meta-regression analysis demonstrated an association between a higher BED and an increased likelihood of response (P = 0.010). Subgroup analyses showed that higher BED categories were associated with higher response rates (P = 0.005). The pooled rebleeding rate was 32.4%. The median overall survival and rebleeding-free survival were 3.8 and 3.4 months, respectively. Radiotherapy was generally well tolerated, with a low incidence of grade ≥ 3 toxicities. CONCLUSIONS: Palliative radiotherapy is an effective and well-tolerated treatment for gastric cancer-related bleeding. Although study-level meta-regression identified a statistical association between higher BED and hemostatic response, this may largely reflect selection bias and methodological limitations rather than a true dose-response relationship. Given the poor prognosis of this population, shorter dose-fractionation regimens are appropriate for many patients, whereas higher-BED regimens remain reasonable for selected patients.

articles.title: MRI-defined parametrial venous invasion in locally advanced cervical cancer: association with pathological venous invasion, pretreatment lymph node metastasis, and survival outcomes.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate MRI-defined parametrial venous invasion (mrPMVI) for detecting pathological parametrial venous invasion (pPMVI) and its associations with pretreatment lymph node metastasis (LNM) and survival outcomes in locally advanced cervical cancer. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 42 patients with cervical cancer with parametrial invasion on MRI or histopathology, corresponding to International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics 2018 stage IIB or higher disease. Fifteen patients underwent surgery without preoperative therapy and were included in the pathological validation analysis. Image interpretation was primarily based on T2-weighted and diffusion-weighted imaging. Two radiologists independently assessed mrPMVI using a five-point scoring system. Scores ≥ 3 were predefined as mrPMVI-positive. Diagnostic performance for pPMVI and interobserver agreement were evaluated. Univariable logistic and Cox regression analyses were performed for pretreatment LNM and survival outcomes, respectively. RESULTS: pPMVI was present in 10 of 15 patients. The five-point mrPMVI score showed an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.87 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.60-0.98) for detecting pPMVI. The predefined threshold (≥ 3) yielded 30.0% sensitivity and 100% specificity. Interobserver agreement for the five-point mrPMVI score was substantial (linearly weighted κ = 0.75). mrPMVI positivity was associated with pretreatment LNM (odds ratio = 4.00, 95% CI: 1.05-15.26, p = 0.042). During a median follow-up of 24.0 months, 16 patients experienced disease progression and 10 died. mrPMVI positivity was associated with shorter progression-free survival (hazard ratio = 34.25, 95% CI: 4.35-269.91; p < 0.001) and overall survival (hazard ratio = 10.16; 95% CI: 1.28-80.61, p = 0.028). CONCLUSION: The mrPMVI score showed potential for identifying pPMVI, although the predefined threshold was highly specific but insensitive. mrPMVI positivity was associated with pretreatment LNM and survival outcomes, suggesting potential complementary value for risk characterization in locally advanced cervical cancer.

articles.title: An Accountable Encounter-Based Imaging Workflow for Point-of-Care Ultrasound: Integrating Image Availability, Clinician Attribution, and Documentation Accountability.
articles.abstract: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) is integral to emergency department (ED) care, but traditional order-based imaging workflows (OBIWs) are poorly aligned with unscheduled encounters and dynamic bedside imaging needs. We describe an accountable encounter-based imaging workflow (EBIW) that integrates patient identification, clinician attribution, encounter-linked image routing, and documentation accountability into a unified imaging informatics architecture. We performed a retrospective observational analysis of aggregated ED POCUS charge data from January 2018 through December 2025 at a single urban academic ED. Three sequential workflows were evaluated: a legacy electronic health record (EHR)-based OBIW, a POCUS Manager-based OBIW, and an accountable EBIW. The accountable EBIW links ultrasound images directly to the ED encounter using barcode-based patient and clinician identification and a centralized Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine (DICOM) router that generates an image availability message. This enables immediate image access in the picture archiving and communication system, EHR, and POCUS management platform before report completion. Charges were not used as a measure of reimbursement or financial return. Because a charge could only be generated after image archival, encounter linkage, documentation, and clinician attestation, charge capture served as a longitudinal system-level marker of completed workflow execution. Charges were normalized by ED visit volume and analyzed using interrupted time series analysis. Transition from the EHR-based OBIW to the POCUS Manager-based OBIW was not associated with an immediate increase in charges. Implementation of the accountable EBIW was associated with an immediate level increase of $11,746 per 1000 visits and a sustained positive quarterly slope thereafter. An accountable EBIW integrating encounter-level acquisition, DICOM routing, immediate image availability, clinician attribution, and documentation accountability was associated with improved capture of ED POCUS utilization.

articles.title: Investigation on Automatic Classification of Bone, Lymph Node, and Local Lesions in CT Images of Prostate Cancer Patients.
articles.abstract: Accurate assessment of different types of prostate cancer (PCa) lesions is a crucial part of treatment planning. Following a computed tomography (CT) or a positron emission tomography (PET)/CT imaging scan, a significant amount of time is required from the clinicians to detect lesions and characterize them by their anatomical locations. To facilitate the development of new image analysis applications, we investigated the potential of automated classification of PCa lesions between bone metastases, lymph node metastases, local lesions, and other PCa lesions in CT images via machine learning (ML) and deep learning models. We annotated a total of 4949 PCa lesions by their type in a private dataset of   18  F-prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) PET/CT images of 532 PCa patients and an external test set of publicly available PSMA PET/CT images from 30 patients. Using information of coordinates of the detected lesions, we automatically extracted 15 different features from the CT and the results of the automated 3D anatomical segmentation tool TotalSegmentator for each lesion, and trained several traditional ML models to classify lesions by their anatomical type. Additionally, we experimented with convolutional neural networks (CNNs) of different dimensionalities with CT and TotalSegmentator inputs. According to our results, the most accurate model was XGBoost with an overall accuracy of 96.0%. It identified bone metastases, lymph node metastases, and local lesions with sensitivities of 97.9±1.2%, 95.2±1.3%, and 93.1±2.8% in the five-fold cross-validation experiments of the primary data and 96.3%, 94.0%, and 80.0% on the external test set, respectively. Conversely, the CNNs underperformed the best ML models in distinguishing local lesions. To conclude, a simple ML model can accurately classify PCa lesions between bone, lymph node, and local lesions based on CT images, lesion locations, and automated anatomical segmentation data, but more research is required for distinguishing PCa lesions outside these categories.

articles.title: Evaluating Explicit Anatomical Priors Beyond a Mature CT Detector for Six Acute Abdominal Emergencies.
articles.abstract: To test whether anatomical priors from a general-purpose organ segmentation model (TotalSegmentator, TS), applied at inference or during training, improve an externally validated YOLOv11 detector for six acute abdominal emergencies. The frozen detector was applied to 827 external Stanford Merlin CT studies with language-model report labels; a nested 280-study radiologist-adjudicated subset was the reference standard. TS-derived slice selection (Arm A), organ-state integration (Arm B), and their combination (Arm C) were compared with the detector alone under frozen, recalibrated, and fine-tuned conditions. The detector was also retrained from scratch (identical 10-epoch budget) with image channels only, with the patient's TS organ maps as added input channels, or with another patient's maps. AUROC was primary; comparisons used a paired study-level bootstrap. The detector generalized externally (macro AUROC 0.816 cohort; 0.879 adjudicated). Slice selection was non-inferior but not beneficial: nearly all confident detections already lay within the anchored organ's axial range; organ-state fusion improved AUROC only for cholecystitis (hypothesis-generating). In single runs, training with organ maps raised internal test mAP@0.5 (0.517 versus 0.482), and the model depended on the maps, but external macro AUROC did not improve (0.822 versus 0.829; Δ -0.007, 95% CI -0.019 to +0.007) and kidney-stone AUROC fell (0.678 versus 0.768; exploratory), unlike with another patient's maps. Per-site recalibration was the most effective operating-point adjustment (macro F1 +0.021); annotation-free fine-tuning reduced discrimination. Explicit anatomy, applied after detection or during training, did not improve this detector's overall external discrimination. Per-site recalibration gave the largest operating-point gain.

articles.title: Diagnosis of Suspected Pituitary Microadenomas: The Complementary Role of Habitat-based Non-enhanced MRI Radiomics Features.
articles.abstract: To develop and validate a combined model for detecting pituitary microadenomas in suspected cases using non-contrast T1-weighted sagittal (T1SAG) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and to assess its performance as a non-contrast imaging-based tool for clinical decision support.This retrospective two-center study enrolled 519 patients with suspected pituitary microadenomas, divided into a training set (n = 321), an internal validation set (n = 80), and an external test set (n = 118). Radiomics features were extracted from both the entire pituitary gland and its habitat subregions, generated via unsupervised K-means clustering. Eight predictive models were constructed using logistic regression: a clinical model, an intra-pituitary radiomics model, three individual habitat models (Habitat 1, 2, and 3), an early-fusion model combining all habitats, an ensemble model integrating the probability outputs of the three habitat models, and a combined model that integrated clinical, intra-pituitary, and the optimal fusion model. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curves (ROC), calibration curves, and decision curve analysis.Among all models, the combined model demonstrated the best predictive performance across all three cohorts, achieving areas under the curve (AUCs) of 0.885 (95% CI: 0.850-0.920) in the training set, 0.788 (95% CI: 0.690-0.885) in the internal validation set, and 0.796 (95% CI: 0.712-0.880) in the external test set. The combined model also achieved the highest accuracy and sensitivity across all datasets.The combined prediction model showed robust performance in distinguishing pituitary microadenomas in suspected cases, offering enhanced clinical decision support while reducing dependence on contrast-enhanced MRI examinations.

articles.title: Building and Validating a Data-Governance Workflow for Artificial Intelligence-Based Tuberculosis Detection from Chest Radiographs, and Quantifying the Impact of Data Leakage.
articles.abstract: Studies applying artificial intelligence (AI) to tuberculosis (TB) detection from chest radiographs (CXR) focus on models and metrics, yet the quality, provenance and reproducibility of the data workflow decide the reliability of results; duplicate images and non-patient-level splitting inflate evaluation metrics. We propose a seven-step data-governance workflow: multi-source standardisation, provenance management, three-hash deduplication (MD5, pHash, dHash), patient-level splitting, invariant-check auditing, lung segmentation and version freezing by data fingerprint. Four leakage scenarios (deduplication on or off; patient-level or random split) were repeated 20 times with paired splits and compared with the clean scenario on per-repeat differences. On 46,410 CXR images from seven public sources, the workflow removed duplicates at file and content level, standardised 16,554 TB Portals DICOM images, generated 34,554 lung masks without failure and sealed every layer with SHA-256 hashes. On the three-class multi-source corpus, the area under the curve (AUC) saturated near 0.997 in every scenario, consistent with source-class confounding; paired leakage effects were statistically detectable but below 0.1 percentage points. On a single-source probe task (drug resistance within TB Portals), random image-level splitting inflated the internal AUC by 1.7 percentage points (95% confidence interval 0.9 to 2.4; p = 0.001), or 1.2 points after a deduplication gap found during revision was repaired; in a holdout design, an internal gap of 1.1 points shrank to 0.4 points on a patient-disjoint holdout. The magnitude of leakage depends on data structure and must be measured; a rigorous governance workflow makes that measurement, and data reuse, verifiable.

articles.title: Advanced diffusion-weighted imaging for evaluating neoadjuvant chemotherapy in breast cancer.
articles.abstract: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) is widely used for locally advanced breast cancer. Imaging monitoring during NAC facilitates timely treatment adjustments and leads to improved patient outcomes. Dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI plays a key role in assessing NAC response; however, early during treatment, tumor volume changes lag behind intracellular microstructural and functional alterations. Diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) provides average tissue diffusion information based on Gaussian water motion but fails to capture intratumoral heterogeneity. Advanced DWI techniques, including intravoxel incoherent motion (IVIM), stretched exponential modeling (SEM), diffusion kurtosis imaging (DKI), diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), and DWI-based virtual magnetic resonance elastography (vMRE), have attracted growing interest in evaluating breast cancer during NAC. These techniques require no gadolinium-based contrast agents and can provide valuable information on tumor microstructure, heterogeneity, and microcirculation. However, a notable gap persists between the potential benefits of advanced DWI and their actual clinical utility. This review assesses the current applications and limitations of advanced DWI techniques in NAC for breast cancer.

articles.title: Multiparametric MRI with amide proton transfer imaging for assessing stromal invasion depth of early- stage cervical cancer.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To explore the value of multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) with amide proton transfer (APT) imaging in assessing the depth of stromal invasion (DSI) in early-stage cervical cancer. METHODS: Clinical and imaging data of patients with early-stage cervical cancer who were pathologically diagnosed at our hospital between January 2020 and June 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. All patients underwent routine MRI, diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), APT imaging, and dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI (DCE-MRI) before treatment. Apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC), APT values, and semi-quantitative DCE-MRI parameters were measured.
